audit.title: Using Data Feeds on Aptos

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong intro — "Chainlink Data Feeds on Aptos provides data through a single price feed contract that handles multiple data feeds" is a liftable canonical statement. Weak: task sections open with process ("In this step, you will…") rather than the answer/API call itself.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Good hierarchy (9 headings, 1 H1, 0 level skips, no section over 600 words per measured facts). Weak: 0 tables — feed IDs, package addresses, and Octas conversions are buried in prose instead of an extractable table.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Strong — real addresses, gas values, `1 APT = 100,000,000 Octas`, 18-decimal precision, live feed ID. Measured facts show 0 numerals carry explicit units in prose; unit annotation would help.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: External links to `aptos.dev`, the Move language, and the Aptos explorer are present, but measured facts flag 0 primary-source links — no link to a Chainlink Data Feeds API/registry reference for `get_benchmarks`.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good Aptos/Move one-liner and the single-contract/feed-ID contrast. Weak: no crisp definition of `Benchmark`, `feed ID`, or the `router`/`registry` modules near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak — measured facts confirm 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, 0 og/twitter tags. Head metadata could not be verified; the CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. 15 fenced blocks, all tagged, imports present, expected outputs shown.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Weak — covers setup→deploy→read, but no troubleshooting/FAQ, no error-string headings, and headings are concept-named rather than phrased as "how do I read a price feed on Aptos".

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent product naming and unambiguous steps.

audit.summary: This is a clean, end-to-end integration tutorial for reading Chainlink Data Feeds from Move contracts on Aptos, with complete runnable code and real on-chain addresses/feed IDs — genuinely strong on code and clarity. Its biggest GEO strength is the complete, tagged, import-bearing Move module plus real testnet addresses; its biggest opportunity is the near-total absence of machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no dates) combined with concept-titled headings ("Getting Started (CLI)") that miss the symptom/how-to queries agents actually type. The Aptos feed API (`get_benchmarks` / `get_benchmark_value`) differs sharply from the EVM `AggregatorV3Interface`/`latestRoundData` idiom the models hold as a prior — this page must defend that difference explicitly or answers will hallucinate the EVM pattern.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/how-to phrased headings and a short FAQ
recommendations.where: section headings ("Getting Started (CLI)", "Interact with the deployed contract") and a new tail section.
recommendations.issue: headings are concept/process-titled; devs query "how to get latest price feed Aptos Move".
recommendations.change: rename/add H3s such as "How to read the latest BTC/USD price on Aptos", "How to find a feed ID on Aptos", and add an FAQ/Troubleshooting block covering common failures (e.g. `INCLUDING DEPENDENCY` git-dep errors, insufficient Octas / faucet funding, `--skip-fetch-latest-git-deps` usage).
recommendations.why: headings phrased as the exact user question win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses, even when the answer is already in the body.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle`, canonical URL, and last-updated date
recommendations.issue: measured facts — 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no dates.
recommendations.change: emit a `TechArticle` block with `headline`, `about` (Chainlink Data Feeds, Aptos, Move), `programmingLanguage: ["Move","bash"]`, a self-referential `canonical`, and a visible `dateModified`.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals raise parse-ability and E-E-A-T trust for engines and agents.

recommendations.title: Lead with the canonical Aptos API and name the EVM pattern as a Don't
recommendations.where: intro and "Write the Move contract" section.
recommendations.issue: page never states that `latestRoundData` / `AggregatorV3Interface` do **not** exist on Aptos.
recommendations.change: add a one-liner: "On Aptos, read feeds with `data_feeds::router::get_benchmarks` then `get_benchmark_value` / `get_benchmark_timestamp` — there is no per-feed `AggregatorV3Interface` or `latestRoundData` as on EVM chains." Lead the contract section with this call rather than "In this step, you will…".
recommendations.why: models default to the EVM idiom from training priors; explicitly naming the wrong pattern blocks the substitution.

recommendations.title: Add a summary table of addresses, networks, and the sample feed ID
recommendations.where: near "Set up your project" / "Interact with the deployed contract".
recommendations.issue: measured facts — 0 tables; `data_feeds`, `platform`, testnet feed ID, mainnet pointer sit in prose.
recommendations.change: a small table: `data_feeds` / `platform` package addresses, network (testnet), BTC/USD feed ID, and link to mainnet Feed Addresses.
recommendations.why: tables are high-extraction units engines lift verbatim into answers.

recommendations.title: Add a primary-source link for the feed API
recommendations.issue: measured facts — 0 primary-source links; the `router`/`registry` functions are unreferenced.
recommendations.change: inline-link to the Chainlink Data Feeds API reference / registry module docs for `get_benchmarks`, `get_benchmark_value`, `get_benchmark_timestamp`.
recommendations.why: attributable API claims raise citation rate and let agents resolve function signatures.

recommendations.title: Add crisp definitions for `Benchmark` and `feed ID`
recommendations.issue: `Benchmark`, `feed ID`, `router`, `registry` used without a one-line definition.
recommendations.change: e.g. "A `Benchmark` is the struct returned per feed, carrying the price value (18 decimals) and the Unix timestamp of the last on-chain update."
recommendations.why: self-contained definitions near first use are verbatim-liftable and improve entity resolution.

antiPatterns: No stale-content signal is present, but also **no visible date** — engines cannot confirm freshness.
Dependency `rev = "main"` in `Move.toml` is a moving target; a pinned commit/tag would improve reproducibility for agents (minor).
No keyword stuffing, marketing fluff, or unresolved cross-references detected.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good; ensure this page is listed in it.
Site-level: confirm canonical URL and `TechArticle` schema are emitted at build time across the docs, not just here.
Freshness cadence: surface a `dateModified` in the rendered page and sitemap so engines can weight recency.
